idea: Sugeno/Mamdani fuzzy controller for an isolated junction with four inputs (traffic density 0-100 with Low 0-30 / Medium 20-70 / High 60-100; average waiting time 0-300 s with Short 0-100 / Moderate 80-200 / Long 160-300; pedestrian crowd 0-60 with Sparse/Moderate/Dense; binary priority condition) and outputs effective green 0-120 s (Short 0-40, Medium 30-90, Long 80-120), total cycle 0-300 s and a lane priority flag; 37 IF-THEN rules; AND = min, OR = max, Sugeno output as rule-strength-weighted average of constants. Worked example: density 50, wait 116, priority -> green 60, cycle 150.
does: Extension signal_override: computes green time per phase from queue density, mean waiting time and a priority flag (bus/EV request from TSP/DEVL) via a small fuzzy rule base, interpretable by reading the fired rules.
inputs: per-approach queue density, mean wait, pedestrian count (if modelled), priority flag
outputs: green time and cycle length per step; list of fired rules with strengths (an explanation)
existing: partial: SCATS/SCOOT planning and TSP signal override; no fuzzy or actuated control
notes: Stdlib-only (trapezoid/triangle membership + weighted average). Its fired-rule list is a built-in explanation, tying in with the XAI ideas. Ranges are for a generic junction and need scaling to metres/vehicles per lane.

idea: Three-sensor congestion detector on a road block: pings at A and B (distance AB known) give each vehicle's speed; expected time to reach C (distance BC) is queued; when a vehicle's actual crossing is later than its estimate by 30 s (and queue length hits the block's capacity N = BC/G) a jam is declared, the average actual crossing time becomes the road weight for rerouting. Also the headway/flow/density algebra Q=N/T, H=1/Q, K=N/S, Q=K*V.
does: Declares congestion on a road in a headless run when vehicles overrun their predicted travel time by a threshold, and reports onset time and duration; the weights feed rerouting.
inputs: vehicle entry/exit timestamps on a road block, entry speed, block length
outputs: jam onset/clear times, road weight (mean actual crossing time)
notes: Simple and robust; the 30 s threshold is a parameter to calibrate. Cheap with the lane-relative vehicle state ACMS already has.

idea: Kerner three-phase classification of each road state from speed, flow and density: Free flow (speed high, flow high, density low), Synchronised flow (speed low, flow close to free-flow value, density middle), Wide moving jam (speed and flow negligible, density highest); on the Q=K*V parabola, left of the capacity peak is free flow, right is congested, and the slope of the line from the origin to the state (speed) separates the two.
does: Labels each road/time bin in results as free, synchronised or jam from mean speed and density, giving share of time in each phase and where jams form and dissolve.
outputs: phase per road per bin, summary share
notes: Thresholds not given in the book; use fractions of free-flow speed and of the measured capacity. Complements Summary tab KPIs.

idea: Road-condition coefficient c in (0,1] divides a road's apparent travel time to give its actual weight (600 s at c=0.5 becomes 1200 s), so a poor village road loses to a longer city road; detour search by A* run recursively until the detour itself is uncongested (Optiflow).
does: Adds a per-road condition factor to route costs and recursion over detours that are themselves congested.
existing: none (road type label stored only, per not_built)
notes: Gives the stored road type label a behaviour, which not_built lists as missing; fold into rolling_reroute.
